full_judgment: 4. Mr. Mohammad Nawab Ali, teamed Advocate-on-Record, appearing for the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in failing to exercise the jurisdiction vested in him by Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and in not interfering with the judgment and decree of reversal as passed by the appellate Court below based on misreading and non-consideration of the evidence on record, particularly, the pieces of documentary evidence, contained in the records of Title Suit Nos.319 of 1961 and 244 of 1966 as also exhibit-7, showing that the mutation Case No.100 of 1970-71 is a fictitious case number and no such case was in existence since in the relevant year only 78 cases in total were filed; that the judgment and order of the appellate Court below, without adverting to the reasons upon which the trial Court decreed the suit, and without proper reversal of the findings of the trial Court, was not a proper judgment of reversal; that the trial Court on correct assessment of the evidence on record and on cogent reasons found that the predecessor-in-interest of the contesting defendants created the impugned decrees and mutation order by practice of fraud, the High Court Division erred in law in not considering the judgment of the two Courts below in juxtaposition with each other and in mechanically affirming the decision of the appellate Court below without applying his judicial mind. The learned Advocate further submitted that the appellate Court below wrongly decided the question of limitation without considering at all the legal effect of fraud and as per Section 18 of the Limitation Act, and fraud having been proved to the hilt the suit was barred by limitation inasmuch as the acts of fraud committed by predecessor-in-interest of the contesting defendants came to light on 10.03.1992 and the suit was filed on 15.11.1994 and as such, the suit was not barred by limitation.
